title: Portfolio Construction
answer: Personalised advice, optimisation, tail risk hedging, sustainability factors and pricing illiquid assets.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice uses AI to tailor portfolio construction to an individual's goals, constraints, tax situation, risk tolerance, and time horizon.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance moves past the Markowitz framework that uses only expected return and volatility.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in AI portfolio construction is the practice of reducing exposure to rare but severe losses that can hit concentrated AI equity, credit, or venture positions.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios refer to environmental, social and governance criteria used alongside financial metrics when selecting and weighting assets, including AI-related instruments.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers positions that do not trade on an active exchange, such as private AI company equity, venture fund interests, restricted stock, intellectual property, data rights, and thinly traded tokens.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning to the practical tasks of building and maintaining an investment portfolio. It includes generating personalised asset mixes from client data, searching for portfolios that balance risk and return beyond simple mean-variance models, and designing hedges against rare but severe losses. It also covers scoring investments on environmental, social and governance factors and estimating prices for assets that rarely trade. The work is descriptive and analytical, not a set of instructions for any individual investor.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most mature parts are optimisation and tail risk hedging, where models can process many constraints and historical scenarios quickly. Personalised advice remains limited by sparse data about each person and by the difficulty of knowing future preferences. Sustainability scoring is inconsistent because definitions and disclosures vary widely. Pricing illiquid assets still depends heavily on assumptions and sparse comparable sales, so outputs are ranges rather than precise values. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which is a small, liquid slice of a much larger and less transparent universe.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how machine learning turns client information into an asset mix should start with Personalised Wealth Advice. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance explains the mathematical shift from simple risk-return tradeoffs to objectives like downside risk, turnover and tax. Tail Risk Hedging covers the specific problem of protecting a portfolio against extreme market moves. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios shows how non-financial criteria are turned into portfolio weights. Pricing Illiquid Assets addresses the hardest valuation problem, where there are few market prices to learn from.
